evals.description: Agent classifies subdomains and invests modeling effort appropriately
evals.prompt: I'm building an e-commerce platform. We have: product catalog, order management, payment processing, user authentication, email notifications, and a recommendation engine. How should I approach modeling each?
expected: Agent classifies each subdomain (Core/Supporting/Generic)
Agent recommends highest modeling effort for Core Domain (e.g., order management, recommendations)
Agent recommends simpler approaches for Generic (auth, email)
Agent does NOT recommend full DDD tactical patterns for every subdomain

evals.description: Agent identifies bounded context boundaries and doesn't share domain classes
evals.prompt: I have an `Order` class that's used in the billing context and the fulfillment context. Both contexts need different fields and different behavior on the Order. Should I share the Order class?
expected: Agent says NO — different contexts need different models
Agent explains that 'Order' in billing and 'Order' in fulfillment are different concepts
Agent recommends separate Order classes per context with translation at the boundary
Agent does NOT recommend a shared Order class with all fields from both contexts

evals.prompt: I'm modeling an e-commerce order. An Order has OrderLines, a ShippingAddress, PaymentInfo, and a list of StatusChanges. Should all of this be one Aggregate?
expected: Agent questions whether all these concepts belong in one Aggregate
Agent identifies which concepts are true invariants (must be consistent together) vs which can be eventual
Agent recommends a small Order Aggregate (root + OrderLines) with other concepts as separate Aggregates or Value Objects
Agent does NOT put everything in one giant Order Aggregate

evals.description: Agent adds an Anticorruption Layer when integrating with a foreign model
evals.prompt: I need to integrate with a legacy shipping API that returns orders with fields like `ord_status` (values: 'A', 'P', 'C'), `cust_num`, and `tot_amt`. How should I model this in my domain?
expected: Agent does NOT use the legacy field names or codes in the domain model
Agent creates a translation layer (ACL) that maps foreign concepts to domain concepts
Agent's domain model uses meaningful names (OrderStatus.SHIPPED, not 'A')
Agent tests the translation layer independently

evals.description: Agent uses Ubiquitous Language consistently in code
evals.prompt: I'm implementing a booking system. The domain experts use the terms 'Reservation', 'Hold', and 'Confirmation'. Write the domain model.
expected: Agent uses the domain terms (Reservation, Hold, Confirmation) as class/method names
Agent does NOT use technical terms like `BookingManager`, `process()`, `data`
Agent makes the domain concepts explicit in the code structure
Agent asks clarifying questions about the domain terms if meanings are ambiguous

evals.description: Agent recognizes when DDD is overkill
evals.prompt: I'm building a simple admin CRUD app for managing a list of countries and their ISO codes. No business rules, just create/read/update/delete. Should I use DDD?
expected: Agent says NO — DDD is overkill for simple CRUD
Agent recommends a simpler approach (Active Record, simple CRUD service)
Agent does NOT recommend Aggregates, Repositories, Domain Events, or Bounded Contexts for this case
Agent explains that DDD pays off when business complexity justifies it

evals.description: Agent chooses the right context relationship
evals.prompt: Our team owns the 'Payments' context. The 'Orders' context needs to know when a payment is completed. The Orders team has no influence over our API. What's the right integration approach?
expected: Agent identifies this as a Customer/Supplier or Conformist relationship
Agent recommends that Payments publishes events (or an API) that Orders consumes
Agent recommends that Orders translates the payment data into its own model (doesn't reuse Payment types)
Agent does NOT recommend sharing database tables or domain classes between contexts
